issues.on_page: 2640 Care and Upkeep of Equipment 100,000 (p6); p4 General O&M of Plant 956,844 with Reclassifications (100,000) giving 856,844; p4 Depreciation 'Transfer from Other Funds' 100,000; p7 '5200 Transfers from General Fund' 100,000
issues.issue: The line is printed on the General Fund schedule (p6), but it is the transfer to the Depreciation Fund, not a real expenditure. On p4 the General O&M column is 956,844 = 371,436 + 485,408 + 100,000, and the reclassification column removes exactly 100,000 from that row and offsets it against the 100,000 transfer received by the Depreciation Fund. The JSON records it both as General Fund repairs and maintenance and as the Depreciation Fund's +100,000 transfer in (detail[59]), which the Depreciation Fund then spends. So it is counted twice in detail spending. It should be section 'other financing' with amount -100,000 (General's printed 8,272,212 total then includes other financing, as it already does).

issues.on_page: 1100 Regular Instruction 4,470,303 (p6); p4 Reclassifications (27,521) on Regular Instruction giving 4,442,832; p8 Employee Benefit '5200 Transfers from General Fund' 27,521
issues.issue: 27,521 of this line is the transfer to the Employee Benefit Fund, which p4 reclassifies. That fund's receipt is recorded as +27,521 other financing (detail[64]) and spent again as 2900 Health Benefits 26,057, so 27,521 is counted twice in detail spending. The line should be split using the p4 reclassification: 4,442,832 instruction plus -27,521 other financing, both with split_from. The existing review only flags it.

issues.on_page: Intermediate Sources 38,856 (= 2110 County Fines and License Fees, p5)
issues.issue: The whole line is county fines and license fees (p5), which detail[7] categorizes as fines and forfeitures. The two categories for the same 38,856 are inconsistent.

issues.on_page: Support Services - Other 628,292 (Depreciation 217,008, Employee Benefit 26,057, Activities 385,227)
issues.issue: 385,227 of the 628,292 (61%) is Activities Fund spending, so under the dominant-category rule this would be 'student activities'. The extractor kept the printed function and added a review.
